key_insight: A shallow variational quantum circuit can learn the quantum phase estimation output distribution analytically from the Dirichlet kernel, avoiding expensive quantum-circuit simulation.
engineering_relevance: This offers a hardware-efficient path to estimate molecular ground-state energies on NISQ devices while keeping circuit depth low enough for near-term quantum hardware.
method: Compute the QPE target distribution classically from the FCI ground-state energy, ancilla count, and evolution time via the Dirichlet kernel.
Train a shallow VQC surrogate and compare entangler layouts, depths, and dynamical decoupling settings on IBM Quantum hardware.
Use distribution metrics to select the best ansatz; then validate energy recovery on H2 under noise and ideal-simulator settings.
evidence_signal: Across four experimental stages, the authors evaluated Hellinger distance, fidelity error, total variation distance, and Jensen-Shannon divergence, and report recovery of the ground-state energy within chemical accuracy.
watch_item: Performance depends on noise, ansatz choice, and depth; the best configuration may not transfer unchanged to larger molecules or different hardware calibrations.
paper_title: An Analytically Trained Variational Surrogate for Quantum Phase Estimation on NISQ Hardware
